name: Employer Nomination Scheme (subclass 186)

requirements.blocker_text: This requires nomination by an approved Australian employer for a position on the eligible occupation list.
requirements.fix_path: Secure a nomination from an approved employer.

requirements.blocker_text: This requires an annual salary of at least $79,423 AUD (2026 Core Skills Income Threshold) or the Annual Market Salary Rate for the role, whichever is higher.
requirements.fix_path: Negotiate a salary meeting the threshold.

requirements.blocker_text: This requires being under 45, unless a specific exemption applies (e.g. high income in 2 of the last 3 years).
This requires having worked for the nominating employer on a Skills in Demand (subclass 482) visa for at least 2 years (streams vary by exact tenure), with continued nomination.

evidence_required.document: Skills assessment where required by occupation

sources.title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186) - Department of Home Affairs

notes: Formula-linked to the same CSIT national variable as au_skills_in_demand_482 — a genuinely clean cross-route formula relationship, similar to how Germany's and Spain's Blue Card/general-work-permit thresholds share a common reference figure. Permanent on grant, same structural pattern as 189/190 — Australia's employer-sponsored PERMANENT route (186) is meaningfully different from its employer-sponsored TEMPORARY route (482), which is provisional and requires a further step to reach permanence, the same distinction seen between 189/190 (direct-permanent) and 491 (provisional) among the points-tested routes. Temporary Residence Transition stream is the natural conversion path from au_skills_in_demand_482 after 2+ years — the direct structural link between Australia's two main employer-sponsored routes, worth surfacing prominently in a Journey view.
